name: Central Media Library For Network Websites
author: Kirtikumar Solanki

sections.description:
Central Media Library For Network Websites enables all subsites in a WordPress multisite network to access and use a shared, centralized media library. This helps prevent media duplication, simplifies media management, and keeps your network more organized.

Features

  • Share a single media library across the entire network.
  • Prevent duplicate uploads across subsites.
  • Lightweight and easy to configure.
  • Newly uploaded media becomes available network-wide.
  • Works in both Grid View and List View.
  • Compatible with featured images.
  • Compatible with Elementor and Elementor Pro.
  • Designed specifically for WordPress multisite networks.
  • Developer-friendly and extendable.

Credits

Developed by Kirtikumar Solanki.

Donations welcome via PayPal.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/central-media-library-for-network-websites/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress dashboard.
  2. Network Activate the plugin via the Plugins menu in your multisite network dashboard.
  3. That’s it! All subsites will now use the central media library from the main site.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin work on single-site WordPress installs?

No. This plugin is built exclusively for WordPress multisite networks.

Which site is used as the central media library?

The main (primary) site of the network acts as the central media hub.

Will this affect existing media files on subsites?

No. Existing files on subsites remain untouched. Only new uploads are directed to the central library.

Can subsites upload new media files?

Yes. Newly uploaded media becomes available in the central library and can be reused across subsites.

Is the plugin compatible with Elementor or page builders?

Yes. The plugin includes fixes for Elementor and Elementor Pro compatibility.

Does it support featured images?

Yes. Media can be selected and used as featured images without issues.

Does it work with List View in the Media Library?

Yes. List View and Grid View are both supported.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Fixed plugin naming issues.
  • Added an update backup warning for safer upgrades.

1.1.9

  • Updated readme and compatibility text for Central Media Manager for Multisite.
  • Added safe attachment metadata handling for propagated central media items.
  • Improved media modal preview support for network sites.
  • Removed legacy type filter from the central library UI to simplify the site experience.
  • Added a backup warning for safe updates.
  • Added UI management from the admin side and network settings.
  • Added a Central Media tab to the plugin sidebar on network websites.

1.1.8

  • Fixed Elementor containers being automatically deleted.

1.1.7

  • Fixed featured image issues in the Classic Editor.
  • Fixed Elementor Pro conflict issues.
  • Improved compatibility with the Classic Editor and Gutenberg Editor.

1.1.6

  • Fixed broken image issues in Elementor Pro 3.3.4.2.

1.1.5

  • Fixed a fatal error in List View.

1.1.4

  • Fixed an issue where featured image data could not be retrieved when uploading an image.
  • Uploaded media is now displayed on the main site and all subsites and can be used across the network.
  • Media files uploaded before plugin activation are also displayed on the respective subsites after the plugin is activated.

1.1.3

  • Fixed a conflict with Elementor.

1.1.2

  • Fixed an issue preventing subsites from using media from the main site.
  • Fixed an issue where media was not visible in List View for non-primary sites.

1.1.1

  • Fixed bugs and improved stability.
  • Updated compatibility for WordPress 6.8.1.

1.0.0

  • Initial plugin release and submission to WordPress.org.
